Nxeon (VPS/game-hosting business, production Next.js app at /opt/nxeon). Three small, independent real admin-panel features requested by the owner from live screenshots tonight.

IMPORTANT PROCESS RULE (a real production outage happened earlier tonight from multiple agents each running their own build/deploy concurrently): **do NOT run `deploy-staging.sh` or `promote-production.sh` yourself.** Before starting, run `ps aux | grep -E "next build|deploy-staging|promote-production"` — if anything is running, wait. Commit and push to `main`, then STOP without deploying. Other agents are concurrently working on unrelated Nxeon features in this same shared tree — check `git status`/`git log` before/after, and if you see uncommitted changes that aren't yours, never `git add -A`, stage only your own files by exact path.

## 1. Audit log: filter by action type

Find the admin Audit Log page (search for "Audit log" / "Last 200 recorded actions" — likely `app/admin/**/audit/page.tsx` or similar). It currently only has a "Staff member" filter dropdown + Filter button. Add a real filter by ACTION TYPE too (the `action` column shows real values like `gameserver.mod.install`, `user.login`, `server.power`, `gameserver.rcon`, etc. — read the actual distinct values live from the `AuditLog` table via a script, don't guess a fixed list) — a dropdown or multi-select populated from real distinct action values in the table, combinable with the existing staff-member filter. Preserve the existing "no impersonated actions" indicator and the 200-row cap unless combining filters would benefit from a higher cap (use judgment, but don't silently change existing behavior without noting it in your report).

## 2. Revenue chart: time-range toggle

Find the admin Operations Overview page (`Live command center for the Nxeon platform` — likely `app/admin/page.tsx` or similar), specifically the "Revenue · last 14 days" card with a small area/line chart. Add real time-range toggle buttons: Today / 7 days / 14 days / 1 month / All time. Each should re-query real revenue data for that window (check whatever query currently backs the 14-day chart and generalize it to accept a date range parameter — real DB aggregation, not client-side slicing of a fixed dataset that only ever fetched 14 days). "All time" should go back to the real first revenue record for this account, not an arbitrary large window. Keep the existing "Orders, renewals and add-ons — refunds and affiliate payouts excluded" framing/methodology exactly as-is, just parameterize the date range.

## 3. Live Chat: clickable customer name + service count

Find the admin Live Chat page (`app/admin/**/live-chat` or similar, "Real-time conversations from the site widget"). When a conversation's participant is a registered customer (not an anonymous visitor), their name in the chat header should be a real clickable link to their customer profile/360 page (check what the Tickets page already does for its "Open customer 360" link — reuse that exact destination/pattern for consistency). Also show their service/server count inline near their name in the header (e.g. "David · davidisawguy@gmail.com · registered customer · 2 servers") — pull the real count from the same query the Clients table or customer-360 page already uses, don't reinvent it.

## Process (mandatory)
- Read the actual current page/component files in full before editing — find them via `grep`/`find`, don't guess paths.
- DB reads only via `db` from `lib/db`, any exploratory scripts under `scripts/_tmp-*.ts` via `npx tsx`, deleted after. NEVER print/construct a raw psql/DATABASE_URL string.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
- Commit and push to `main` (one commit per feature is fine).
- Add a dated entry to `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`.

Report back: exact file paths for each of the three features, confirmation the audit-log action list is populated from REAL distinct values (not hardcoded), confirmation the revenue chart re-queries real data per range (not a client-side slice), and confirmation of the real customer-360 link reused for Live Chat.

**Quality gate: `downloads_total > 1000`** — the same numeric floor `import-modrinth-catalog.ts`
uses. Checked live where it lands: corekeeper 194/312, sandstorm 560/773, mordhau 801/1435. Tried a

how many rows it would add beyond the downloads floor for all 4 games: corekeeper 0, sandstorm 0,
mordhau 1, spaceengineers 0. Not a real gain; not implemented, per the same finding
`import-thunderstore-catalog.ts` already documented for `rating_score`.

**Space Engineers needed an extra content-type filter, Modrinth-`environment`-style.** Its mod.io
catalogue is 165,922 items but 87% (144,710) are `Blueprint`-tagged personal ship designs — not server
mod content at all. Real per-tag totals checked live: Blueprint 144,710, World 16,945, ingameScript
744, scenario 37, **Mod 3,113** — only `tags=Mod` is genuinely "install this on my dedicated server"
content (loaded via the game's real `Mods=` list). This script imports `tags=Mod` only for Space
Engineers; the 1000-download floor then lands at 1,170/3,113. The other 3 games' tag taxonomies have
no comparable non-installable majority bucket (checked live) so no equivalent filter applies to them.

**Category** derived from each game's own live tag taxonomy (`GET /v1/games/{id}/tags`), not
fabricated: corekeeper from its "Type" group (Visual/Audio/Item/NPC/QoL/Overhaul/Language/Library),
sandstorm from its "Mods" group (Total Conversion/Custom Theater/Game Mode/Mutator — a map with no

### 2026-09-20 — Three admin-panel features: audit-log action filter, revenue time-range toggle, live-chat customer link

Three small, independent admin features from live screenshots.

**1. Audit log: filter by action type.** `app/admin/audit/page.tsx`. The page already had a "Staff
member" dropdown; added a second "Action type" dropdown, combinable with it. The option list is a
live `db.auditLog.findMany({ distinct: ["action"], ... })` query run on every render — never a
hardcoded list, so a newly introduced `audit()` call site appears here automatically. Checked live
against production: 79 distinct actions across 2,204 rows (`gameserver.mod.install`, `user.login`,
`server.power`, `gameserver.rcon`, etc.) via a one-off `scripts/_tmp-audit-actions.ts`, deleted after
confirming. The two filters combine with `AND` in the `where` clause. **Behavior change, noted per
process:** the row cap is 200 with no filter applied (unchanged) but 1000 once either filter is set —
a filtered query is already selective, so the old 200-row cap was leaving real history on the table
for something as narrow as "this one employee" or "this one action type". The "no impersonated
actions" badge and the impersonation-attribution logic are untouched.

**2. Revenue chart: time-range toggle.** `app/admin/page.tsx` (Operations Overview, "Revenue" card),
new `lib/admin-metrics.ts` export `revenueSeriesForRange(range)`, new route
`app/api/admin/revenue-chart/route.ts`, new client component `components/admin/RevenueRangeChart.tsx`.
The old inline 14-day-only day-bucketing block (a `dayKey` helper plus a hand-rolled `Map`) is gone;
`revenueSeriesForRange` is now the one place that turns a `RevenueRange` (`today` | `7d` | `14d` |
`1m` | `all`) into a real, range-scoped `db.walletTransaction.findMany` against `REVENUE_WHERE` —
the exact same revenue definition (orders/renewals/add-ons; refunds and affiliate payouts excluded)
used everywhere else. Bucketing granularity adapts to the span (hourly for Today, daily up to ~90
days, weekly up to ~18 months, monthly beyond that) so the chart stays readable at any range.
"All time" resolves `since` from the real first `REVENUE_WHERE` row ever posted for the account —
not an arbitrary lookback window. The page's own SSR render calls `revenueSeriesForRange("14d")` for
the default view (zero extra request on first paint); picking a different button in
`<RevenueRangeChart/>` fetches `/api/admin/revenue-chart?range=...`, which calls the same function —
so every range, including the default, shares one query path. Confirmed this is real per-range
DB aggregation, not a client-side slice of a fixed 14-day dataset, by reading the route handler and
`revenueSeriesForRange` together: the only data ever sent to the browser is the bucketed totals for
the requested window. Note: `RevenueRangeChart.tsx` deliberately duplicates the tiny `RevenueRange`
type + label list locally instead of importing them from `lib/admin-metrics.ts` — that module pulls
in `db` (Prisma) and is server-only; importing it from a `"use client"` file would pull Prisma into
the browser bundle.

**3. Live chat: clickable customer name + service count.** `lib/actions-chat.ts` (both
`listConversations` and `getConversation`), `components/admin/ChatDeskView.tsx`,
`components/admin/ChatInbox.tsx`. Added a `serverCount: number | null` field to the inbox
conversation shape, resolved via a new `resolveServerCounts()` helper (`lib/actions-chat.ts`) — the
exact same `_count.select.servers` relation-count technique
`components/admin/SupportTicketView.tsx` already uses for its "Servers" row, reused rather than
reinvented so Tickets and Live Chat agree on what "N servers" means for a customer. `null` for an
anonymous visitor with no linked account. The thread header in `ChatInbox.tsx` now links the
customer's name to `/admin/users/${userId}` (identical destination/pattern to
`SupportTicketView.tsx`'s "Open customer 360 →" link) whenever `userId` is set, and the meta line
reads e.g. "David · davidisawguy@gmail.com · registered customer · 2 servers" instead of just
"· registered customer". `ChatDeskView.tsx`'s own separate SSR query (used for the very first paint,
before the client starts polling `listConversations`) got the identical treatment so the count is
never missing on first load.

**1. Audit log action filter** — `/opt/nxeon/app/admin/audit/page.tsx`
- Added a second "Action type" `<select>`, combinable (AND) with the existing staff filter.
- Populated from `db.auditLog.findMany({ distinct: ["action"], ... })` — a live query run on every render, never a hardcoded list. Verified via a throwaway `scripts/_tmp-audit-actions.ts` (deleted after) that production currently has **79 distinct actions across 2,204 rows** (`gameserver.mod.install`, `user.login`, `server.power`, `gameserver.rcon`, etc.).
- Behavior change I made and am flagging per instructions: the 200-row cap is unchanged when no filter is applied, but raised to **1000** once either filter is set (a filtered query is already selective, so 200 was leaving real history on the table).
- "no impersonated actions" badge and impersonation-attribution logic untouched.

**2. Revenue chart time-range toggle** — `/opt/nxeon/app/admin/page.tsx`, `/opt/nxeon/lib/admin-metrics.ts` (new `revenueSeriesForRange`), `/opt/nxeon/app/api/admin/revenue-chart/route.ts` (new), `/opt/nxeon/components/admin/RevenueRangeChart.tsx` (new)
- Today / 7 days / 14 days / 1 month / All time buttons. Each click hits `/api/admin/revenue-chart?range=...`, which calls `revenueSeriesForRange(range)` — a real, range-scoped `db.walletTransaction.findMany` against the existing `REVENUE_WHERE` (orders/renewals/add-ons; refunds and affiliate payouts excluded — methodology text kept verbatim). This is **not** a client-side slice of a fixed 14-day dataset: the old inline `dayKey`/`Map` bucketing block was removed entirely, and the page's own SSR default now also calls `revenueSeriesForRange("14d")`, so the default view and every toggle share one query path.
- "All time" resolves `since` from the real first `REVENUE_WHERE` transaction ever posted for the account (`db.walletTransaction.findFirst(...orderBy asc)`), not an arbitrary window.
- Bucketing granularity adapts (hourly for Today, daily ≤90 days, weekly ≤~18 months, monthly beyond) so long ranges stay readable.
- Note: the client component intentionally re-declares the tiny `RevenueRange` type/label list locally rather than importing from `lib/admin-metrics.ts`, since that module imports `db` (Prisma) and must not enter the client bundle.

**3. Live Chat customer link + service count** — `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-chat.ts`, `/opt/nxeon/components/admin/ChatDeskView.tsx`, `/opt/nxeon/components/admin/ChatInbox.tsx`
